title: Requirements register — every capability in the brief, with delivery status
rule: Status is judged on what is actually in the repository and running on this site, not on what the plan says. 'blocked' names the specific missing input.

requirements.requirement: Collect and organise a full list of requirements
requirements.where: data/s2/requirements.json, rendered at s2/pages/requirements.html; the root register data/requirements.json renders at requirements.html
requirements.note: 19 requirements decomposed from the brief, each with an owner and a verification line. PATH CORRECTED 2026-11-16 by session arena/ba29c641 (flag F60 in the root register): this row used to read 'data/requirements.json rendered on Requirements page' when no such file existed, so the repository's only requirements register pointed at an absent path. The file now does exist - a later pass built the root register at data/requirements.json, rendered at requirements.html - so both registers are named here rather than one being silently repointed, and the annex's own copy is named first because it is the one this page renders.
The resolver, ASIN validator, staleness rule and PA-API client are implemented and unit-tested; they gate hard on missing credentials so they never emit invented data.

Requires a valid ASIN set and a trend signal source. No trend value is asserted anywhere on the site. PRECISION 2026-11-16 by session arena/ba29c641: the earlier reason given here - 'no public demand metric exists' - was too strong. A listing page does carry a rank line (Best Sellers Rank, read for all three ASINs on 2026-11-16), and it is point-in-time, per-ASIN and not a history. The row stays blocked on this site's own reading of IP License section 2(e), which keeps Amazon-served figures out of republished tables, and because a trend needs a series that nothing here holds. What changed is the reason: a decision not to publish, not an absence of data.
requirements.source_label: IP License §2(e) and the absence of any public rank history

requirements.note: Conversion rate is an Amazon-reported metric available only in the Associates dashboard for an existing account.
requirements.source_label: Participation Requirements — conversion data lives in Associates Central

requirements.note: Prices may only be shown if served by Amazon in the link or pulled from Creators/PA API, and no product was identifiable.
No rating or review count could be read from any official page for the supplied identifiers.
requirements.source_label: the catalog page that would have held the rating

requirements.note: The competitive model, its inputs and its data sources are specified; the scoring function is implemented and tested on fixtures. It has no real inputs to score.

Rate table read verbatim on 2026-11-16 with no login (Standard Commission Income Statement, Table 1): 'Physical Books, Kitchen, Automotive - 4.50%', 'Home - 3.00%', 'All Other Categories - 4.00%'. The blocker is NOT a login-gated rate card - that wording, and the F-04 reference supporting it, were corrected in the annex's own flags register and this row had not caught up. The genuine gap is narrower: Table 1 is keyed to commission categories and Amazon publishes no ASIN-to-category mapping, so a per-product rate cannot be stated from any public document. Economics are therefore expressed as a formula with the rate as an input, both candidate rows are shown, and no rate is asserted for a specific ASIN.
requirements.source_label: Standard Commission Income Statement, Table 1 (public; read 2026-11-16)

requirements.note: The generator, the fact-check gate (no sentence without a source) and the disclosure injector are implemented and tested. No article is published, because there is no verified product to write about.
Comparison template enforces the lowest-new/lowest-used display rule from Participation Requirements §2(b). Unfilled pending valid ASINs.
Guide template implemented; needs a verified candidate set before it emits anything.
Niche scoring rubric defined and implemented with weights disclosed. No niche is labelled profitable on this site.
Publishing requires the operator's own Associates ID; a tagged Special Link cannot be constructed without it, and republishing the supplied short link is prohibited. See F-01 and F-08.
Measurement plan defined with an explicit prohibition on per-user sub-tagging, per Participation Requirements §2(b). See F-11.
Scheduled re-verification, staleness expiry and a change-detection loop are specified and stubbed with tests; they require credentials and a live URL to run against.
Idempotent pipeline, schema-validated data files, CI build gate, and a per-ASIN design that does not change shape as the catalogue grows.
Each row carries a source URL and a status; blanks are structural, not editorial.
